title: The Iron Bridge
premise: In the winter of the great storms, widowed lighthouse keeper Paloma Pemberton finds a child abandoned at her door with a note: forget the face. The child, Wren, carries a hidden ledger linking the town's iron bridge project to embezzlement by the powerful Harrow family, who built their fortune on Paloma's late husband's drowned workshop. As ice cracks on the river and the bridge—built with stolen funds—begins to fail, Paloma must choose between safety and truth. She finishes her husband's final unfinished work, exposes the Harrows at the bridge's collapse hearing, and claims an unexpected found family with Wren and the bridge workers who shelter them.
about_author: Juniper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs from the storm-battered northern coast. Their fiction blends meticulous historical detail with quiet, stubborn characters who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: The Knock in the Gale
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During the worst storm in living memory, Paloma tends the light alone, grieving her husband Edmund's death the previous spring. A knock reveals a soaked child, Wren, clutching a sealed oilcloth packet, left with only the words 'forget the face.' Emotional beat: guarded grief cracked open by reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Packet Held
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Against her instinct for low profile, she opens the packet: a ledger of payments routed through Edmund's old workshop into the Harrow family's bridge accounts. Wren refuses to say whose child they are. Emotional beat: dread as Paloma realizes the face she was told to forget belongs to someone dangerous.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, shifting to Wren's in the second half. Paloma visits Edmund's derelict riverside workshop, finding his unfinished final commission—a replacement bridge truss design. Wren begins helping, hands busy like hers. Emotional beat: tentative trust forming through shared labor; first hint that Wren recognizes the workshop.

chapters.title: Mr. Harrow Calls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Aldous Harrow visits the lighthouse under polite pretense of storm damage assessment, probing about strangers on the coast. His son Cass watches Wren too closely. Paloma lies smoothly for the first time in years. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into defiance; power shown smiling.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sent to town for supplies, Wren overhears Harrow foremen discussing the bridge's flawed iron and a plan to blame any failure on Edmund Pemberton's 'shoddy' designs. Wren flees, pursued, and is hidden by bridge worker Tomas Okafor. Emotional beat: terror transformed into resolve—the child chooses a side.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying Rope
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tomas and two other workers take refuge at the lighthouse, becoming an unlikely household. They compare the ledger against the workshop plans and confirm the theft. But a traitor among the crew has signaled Harrow. Emotional beat: warmth of found family shadowed by betrayal closing in.

chapters.title: The Fire at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The workshop burns in the night; Paloma races the tide to save Edmund's truss drawings, burning her hands. Cass Harrow watches from the bluff without intervening. The ledger survives inside the lighthouse. Emotional beat: devastating loss transmuted into fury—she will finish the work regardless.

chapters.title: Finishing the Work
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the lighthouse lamp room, Wren and Paloma reconstruct Edmund's design from memory, charred fragments, and Wren's own recollection of watching it drawn. They discover the flaw proving the bridge will fail at spring thaw—and that Wren is Edmund's unacknowledged grandchild. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance braided together; purpose found.

chapters.title: The Day the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the river opening ceremony, the ice groans and the center span sags. Paloma publicly presents the ledger and finished design before the assembled town as the bridge groans; workers evacuate it deliberately, letting it fall harmlessly as proof. Harrow's men seize Wren; Tomas intervenes. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken aloud as the corrupted structure comes down.

chapters.title: The Light We Keep
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Months later: Harrows ruined by inquiry, the town commissions Edmund's true design, and Paloma keeps the light with Wren, Tomas, and the crew as household. On the child's door she once answered, a new sign hangs: home. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance reclaimed not as blood or money but as work shared and kept.
